Name: π₀.₇
1-line summary: 5B-param steerable VLA that gets zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer mostly through scale, metadata conditioning, and world-model/subgoal-image style steering.

Name: DreamZero
Tags: Massive Pre-training; Cross-Embodiment; World Model; Video Prediction; Zero-shot
1-line summary: 14B WAM that jointly generates future frames and actions; useful because the policy is also a prediction engine, so prediction honesty becomes measurable.

Name: GR00T
Tags: Massive Pre-training; Cross-Embodiment; Latent Action Space; Humanoid
1-line summary: Dual-system humanoid VLA with Eagle-2 + DiT action flow model, per-embodiment adapters, and a large data pyramid; strong native humanoid baseline but not automatically strongest on DROID/Agilex-style adaptation.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: CLAP
Tags: Massive Pre-training; Cross-Embodiment; Latent Action Space; Contrastive Learning
1-line summary: Contrastive latent action pretraining that aligns human video and robot action trajectories; interesting because it tries to make human video useful without pretending pixels alone are enough.

Name: LPS
Tags: Latent Action Space; World Model; Online Adaptation; Planning
1-line summary: Uses a pretrained world model/value setup to steer an embodiment-specific policy at inference; does not solve action translation by itself, but is a clean reference for planning as a wrapper.

Name: Zero-shot World Models
1-line summary: Sparse temporally-factored video predictor that extracts depth, segmentation, and optical flow zero-shot through perturb-and-compare style causal inference.

Name: On-the-Fly VLA Adaptation
Tags: World Model; Online Adaptation; Test-time RL
1-line summary: Test-time RL for adapting VLAs online with world-model critics; useful adjacent work, but mostly same-embodiment rather than clean cross-embodiment transfer.

Name: π₀
Tags: Massive Pre-training; Flow Matching; Action Expert; Robot Data
1-line summary: PI's first major flow-matching VLA: big robot data, VLM backbone, and continuous action chunks for dexterous control. Important baseline for why action experts beat token-only action heads.

Name: π₀.₅
Tags: Massive Pre-training; Open-world Generalization; Hierarchical Control
1-line summary: Open-world mobile manipulation VLA that leans hard on diverse home data, high-level subtask prediction, and post-training; strongest practical baseline for prompt/image faithfulness tests.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: π*₀.₆ / RECAP
1-line summary: PI iteration that adds experience-based RL/post-training and shows throughput gains on real tasks; important because it makes online adaptation look practical but expensive.

Name: RLT / RL Token
Tags: Online RL; RL Token; VLA Features; Expert Data
1-line summary: Bootstraps online off-policy RL from frozen VLA features and a learned RL token; useful but not expert-free, so it changes what we can claim about no-data adaptation.

Name: MolmoAct2
1-line summary: Action reasoning model that mixes discrete action-token training with continuous action deployment; the DROID variant is directly relevant for PolaRiS/MolmoSpaces tests.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: MolmoSpaces
1-line summary: Open simulated ecosystem for DROID-style manipulation/navigation; useful because success is not saturated and prompt/camera perturbations expose real policy brittleness.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: Datasets and Environments Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: DROID
Tags: Dataset; Real Robot Data; DROID-style Franka
1-line summary: Large in-the-wild Franka dataset/platform: trajectories, camera views, proprio, actions, language. It is data, not an environment, but it defines the distribution for pi0.5-DROID/MolmoAct2-DROID/DreamZero-DROID.

Name: PolaRiS
1-line summary: DROID-aligned sim/eval stack; the immediate place to debug whether our DROID policies fail because of model limits, camera/action mismatch, or task distribution.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: Datasets and Environments Report; Feasible Experiments and Compute Report

Name: OpenVLA
1-line summary: Open-source VLA baseline with autoregressive action-token style decoding; useful mainly as a public baseline and as a contrast to action-expert/flow-policy designs.

Name: Octo
1-line summary: Open-source generalist robot policy trained on broad trajectory data; useful as a data-scale baseline but less central to the prediction-honesty question.

Name: RT-2
1-line summary: Classic web-to-robot VLA reference: maps internet-scale VLM knowledge into robot action tokens; important background for why token-centric action prediction was compelling early.

Name: Cosmos Policy
Tags: World Model; Video Diffusion; Planning; Value Model
1-line summary: Fine-tunes Cosmos video models into policy/world/value roles; cleaner than DreamZero for action-conditioned planning, but still a heavier stack than our immediate frozen-model probes.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: Fast-WAM
Tags: World Action Model; Auxiliary Video Training; No Test-time Imagination
1-line summary: Wan2.2-based WAM that uses future-video prediction during training but removes imagination at inference; important negative control for whether video objectives matter more than planning.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: LingBot-VA
Tags: World Action Model; Causal Modeling; Video-Action Tokens
1-line summary: Causal WAM that interleaves video/action tokens and decodes actions through inverse dynamics; strong RoboTwin/LIBERO numbers but still very data- and benchmark-dependent.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: Robustness Study
1-line summary: Compares VLAs and WAMs on LIBERO-Plus/RoboTwin-Plus; key takeaway is that clean success is cheap, perturbation robustness is where the actual ranking changes.

Name: Genie Envisioner / GE
Tags: World Model; GE-Act; GE-Sim; EWMBench; Cross-Embodiment
1-line summary: Three-part stack: video world model, action decoder, and action-conditioned neural simulator. Useful because it separates world priors from embodiment-specific action heads.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: Reconstruction or Semantics
Tags: Semantic Latents; World Model Evaluation; JEPA
1-line summary: Shows semantic/action-relevant latents beat pixel-reconstruction latents for useful robotic world models; directly motivates using JEPA-style features for prediction-vs-reality mismatch.

Name: VLA-JEPA
Tags: JEPA; Latent World Model; Human Video; DROID
1-line summary: Adds a latent JEPA-style world model to VLA training; useful because it makes the case for semantic latent prediction without requiring pixel-perfect reconstruction.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: VLA-WAM Training Methodology Report; Benchmarks and Robustness Report

Name: JEPA Physical Planning
1-line summary: JEPA rollout/scoring paper where latent prediction is used for physical planning; useful reference for comparing predicted trajectories to desired/observed trajectories.

Name: Joint Embedding vs Reconstruction
1-line summary: Theory reference for why joint-embedding prediction can be better than reconstruction when nuisance variation dominates; helps justify semantic-space residuals.

Name: V-JEPA 2
1-line summary: Self-supervised video model line behind several semantic-latent arguments; useful as the representation substrate, less directly a robot policy paper.

Name: Demo-JEPA
1-line summary: Demo-conditioned JEPA robotics reference; likely useful for the idea of comparing predicted and observed transitions in latent space.

Name: Any2Any
1-line summary: Humanoid whole-body transfer paper that separates kinematic alignment from dynamics adaptation; useful future reference for arm-to-arm and eventually arm-to-humanoid morphology transfer.
Paper Review Link: Obsidian: Future Experiment - Arm-to-Arm Embodiment Transfer via EEF Adapters

Name: CEI
1-line summary: Unified 3D interface for cross-embodiment visuomotor policy learning; needs deeper pass before we rely on it.

Name: MEM
1-line summary: Multi-scale embodied memory for VLAs; probably relevant to long-horizon context, but still needs a proper read.

Name: Universal Actions
1-line summary: Universal action representation paper; likely relevant to making residual/action tokens less embodiment-specific, but not yet audited deeply.

Name: Mirage
1-line summary: Cross-embodiment transfer by visually replacing robots/cross-painting; useful baseline for observation-adapter ideas.

Name: Flow Policy Gradients
1-line summary: RL/optimization method for flow-policy robot control; relevant if we turn the residual-action head into trainable control.

Name: Flow Matching Policy Gradients
1-line summary: Flow matching plus policy-gradient method; likely useful for later training, not immediate frozen-model diagnostics.

Name: Dreamer 4
Tags: World Model; RL in Imagination; Minecraft
1-line summary: Large-scale world model agent trained inside imagination; useful as a cost/scaling reference more than a robotics baseline.

Name: LeWorldModel
1-line summary: Stable end-to-end JEPA-style latent world model; adjacent to the semantic-latent residual direction.

Name: Reward-Free Latent Dynamics Planning
1-line summary: Planning from reward-free offline data; useful background for unsupervised latent dynamics and value-free planning.

Name: PointWorld
1-line summary: 3D scene benchmark / world-model substrate paper; more environment understanding than policy, but relevant to open-world spatial grounding.

Name: Sim2Real-AD
1-line summary: Autonomous-driving sim-to-real reference; useful mostly for stack design, less directly for robot arm experiments.
